hero.description: RadiantWaves Media brings you the latest developments in energy security, Iran–US diplomacy, the war in Ukraine, European affairs, global markets and Africa.

breaking: MIDDLE EAST: Iran says its proposal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz within seven days remains on the table, subject to US acceptance of its conditions. Negotiations remain unresolved.
ENERGY: Brent crude fell around 2% to approximately $107.57 a barrel in early Monday trading, while security risks around Hormuz continue to affect shipping and investor sentiment.
MARITIME SECURITY: Iran's Revolutionary Guard said an oil tanker caught fire after striking a naval mine in the Strait of Hormuz. The incident and its circumstances require careful monitoring.
UKRAINE: President Volodymyr Zelenskyy says discussions with US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner are continuing as diplomatic efforts proceed.
GLOBAL MARKETS: Investors are assessing uncertainty over US policy towards Russian oil exports, maritime risks and the outlook for technology companies.

FRANCE: Protests over living costs and public services have placed renewed pressure on the government, while President Emmanuel Macron has retained Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez, according to reports.

featured.title: Strait of Hormuz: Diplomacy Continues as Shipping Risks Remain High
featured.content: Iran has reiterated an offer to reopen the Strait of Hormuz within seven days if Washington accepts conditions that include easing restrictions on Iranian oil exports and ports. The United States has also pressed Iran over its nuclear programme, leaving major differences unresolved. The waterway is a vital route for global energy supplies. A reported tanker explosion has added to concerns about the safety of commercial shipping. There is no confirmed comprehensive agreement to end the crisis.

articles.title: Iran Renews Proposal to Reopen Strait of Hormuz
articles.summary: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araqchi says Tehran's offer to reopen the strategic waterway within seven days remains active. The proposal is conditional, and negotiations remain stalled over sanctions, maritime restrictions and Iran's nuclear programme.
articles.content: The Strait of Hormuz remains at the centre of international diplomatic and economic concerns. Iran wants the immediate reopening of the waterway to be a priority, while US officials have demanded action on nuclear enrichment. The outcome could influence oil availability, shipping costs, insurance premiums and inflation. Neither a comprehensive settlement nor a lasting reopening agreement has been confirmed.

articles.title: Reported Tanker Explosion Raises Maritime Security Concerns
articles.summary: Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps said a tanker caught fire after striking a naval mine in the Strait of Hormuz. The incident comes amid continuing risks to vessels navigating the region.
articles.content: The report adds to concerns about the safety of commercial shipping in one of the world's most important energy corridors. Ship operators, insurers and governments are monitoring the situation as attacks and maritime incidents continue to affect confidence. Details about the incident and any wider consequences should be treated cautiously until independently established.
articles.imageQuery: oil tanker at sea Persian Gulf maritime security patrol
articles.source: Reuters reporting carried by international media

articles.title: Oil Prices Ease as Traders Weigh Supply Risks
articles.summary: Brent crude fell to around $107.57 a barrel in early Monday trading as investors weighed regional tensions, potential changes in Russian oil exports and recent price movements.
articles.content: Oil markets remain highly sensitive to developments involving Iran, the Strait of Hormuz and sanctions on Russian energy exports. Even when futures prices fall, shipping risks and insurance costs can keep physical delivery expensive. Sustained disruption could feed into petrol, diesel, electricity, transport and food prices. Market prices fluctuate throughout the day and the quoted figure is an early-session snapshot, not a closing price.

articles.title: France Faces Renewed Pressure Following Protests
articles.summary: Reports describe widespread unrest and arrests following protests linked to living costs and public services. President Emmanuel Macron has declined Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez's offer to resign.
articles.content: The protests have renewed attention on household purchasing power, public services, policing and government accountability. Authorities have announced security responses in affected areas. The scale and consequences of the unrest continue to develop, and reported arrest figures should be understood in the context of ongoing official updates. The economic pressures behind the demonstrations remain an important issue for households and businesses.
articles.imageQuery: Paris France city street demonstration police public square
articles.source: The Guardian live reporting, with developments attributed to officials and news agencies

articles.title: Energy Security Remains a Major Concern Across Europe
articles.summary: Uncertainty surrounding Middle Eastern supplies and maritime routes continues to put pressure on Europe's energy outlook and industrial costs.
articles.content: European governments face the challenge of maintaining reliable energy supplies while protecting households and industry from price volatility. Higher costs for fuel and transport can spread through manufacturing, agriculture and food distribution. Policymakers must balance short-term support with public finances, energy efficiency and long-term supply resilience.

articles.title: Zelenskyy Says Contact With US Envoys Continues
articles.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said he had spoken with US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner as diplomatic communication continues over the war with Russia.
articles.content: The discussions form part of continuing efforts to explore diplomatic initiatives while fighting and attacks on infrastructure remain concerns. Ukraine's relationship with Washington is important to its defence and intelligence support. There is no basis to describe these contacts alone as a peace agreement or a confirmed comprehensive energy ceasefire.

articles.title: Global Investors Assess Russian Oil Policy and Shipping Risks
articles.summary: Financial markets are weighing uncertainty over US measures affecting Russian oil exports, maritime security risks and the outlook for major technology companies.
articles.content: Changes in energy sanctions can affect the availability of crude, trade flows and market expectations, although the practical impact of any policy change may take time to emerge. Investors are also watching technology earnings and the costs associated with artificial intelligence. Bond yields, currencies and equity markets may respond differently as new information becomes available.
articles.imageQuery: global financial markets stock exchange trading screens

articles.title: China Reports 4.5% Economic Growth in Third Quarter
articles.summary: China reported year-on-year economic growth of 4.5% in the third quarter, alongside a reported increase in retail sales, providing investors with fresh information about the world's second-largest economy.
articles.content: The figures offer a snapshot of activity in China as businesses and investors assess domestic demand, manufacturing, trade and technology investment. Growth figures alone do not show how evenly economic gains are distributed among households and industries. Global markets will continue to watch Chinese consumption, exports and policy decisions.
articles.imageQuery: Shanghai China financial district skyline modern skyscrapers

articles.title: AI Investment Remains in Focus as Markets Watch Tech Earnings
articles.summary: Investors are watching major technology-company earnings and the substantial spending associated with artificial intelligence infrastructure.
articles.content: AI continues to influence investment in data centres, chips, cloud computing and software. Companies face questions about whether future revenue will justify the cost of building and operating these systems. This week's earnings announcements may provide additional information, but market expectations and forecasts are not guarantees of future performance.
articles.imageQuery: artificial intelligence data centre server racks technology infrastructure

articles.title: Nigeria's Energy Position Remains Important to African Markets
articles.summary: Nigeria's refining capacity and petroleum exports remain relevant as international fuel markets experience disruption and price volatility.
articles.content: Nigeria's domestic refining sector could contribute to regional fuel supply, but the effect on consumers depends on crude prices, operating costs, distribution, exchange rates and domestic pricing conditions. Higher international energy prices can also affect African countries that depend heavily on imported petroleum products. Claims about current production, export volumes or pump prices should be checked against the latest company and market data.

articles.title: African Households Remain Exposed to Energy and Transport Costs
articles.summary: Changes in oil prices, freight charges and fertiliser supplies can affect transport, food production and household purchasing power across African economies.
articles.content: The effects of international conflicts are not confined to the countries involved. Fuel and shipping costs can increase the price of moving goods, operating machinery and importing essential supplies. Governments and businesses are therefore monitoring energy security, local production, logistics and targeted support for vulnerable households.

morningSummary: Monday's global picture is dominated by energy security, maritime risks and unsettled diplomacy. Iran says it is still offering a conditional route to reopening the Strait of Hormuz, while a reported tanker explosion has raised fresh concerns about shipping safety. Oil prices eased in early trading, but risks to physical supplies and transport remain. In Europe, France is facing renewed pressure following protests, while Ukraine and US envoys continue diplomatic contact. Markets are also assessing uncertainty around Russian oil policy, Chinese growth and major technology-company investment.
